subject.title: Feature request: first-class Telegram reaction triggers for agent wake-up and execution

question: Should Telegram reaction controls use the shared `notificationWake.reactions` policy from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/83611, a Telegram-specific `reactionSemantics` contract like the open fork PR, or a narrower first step?
rationale: The issue asks for new public wake/config semantics and per-reaction meaning, and current open PRs implement overlapping API shapes that automation should not choose without maintainer direction.

options.title: Adopt Shared Wake Policy
options.body: Use the shared queue/wake/off notification wake contract as the canonical base, then layer Telegram reaction keys or semantics only if maintainers still want per-emoji policy.

options.title: Choose Telegram Semantics
options.body: Pursue a Telegram-specific `reactionSemantics` configuration that maps standard and custom emoji to queue, wake, or ignore behavior, accepting a channel-specific contract first.

options.title: Defer First-Class Reactions
options.body: Keep reactions as passive system events for now and pause or close implementation PRs until the product surface is ready.

recommendation.title: Adopt Shared Wake Policy
recommendation.body: Use the shared queue/wake/off notification wake contract as the canonical base, then layer Telegram reaction keys or semantics only if maintainers still want per-emoji policy.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the open shared-policy PR and has the clearest recent history across the Telegram reaction handler and wake-policy surface.
